gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-manrope: Dignified from the first line, Noto Serif Malayalam swells gently on its curves and lets its lowercase stand nearly as tall as the capitals. Manrope then keeps a single pen width throughout, so its bright open curves feel friendly beside the heavier voice above.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-montserrat: Noto Serif Malayalam swells softly in every rounded letter, and its lowercase rivals the capitals in presence. Montserrat is the opposite, its generous white space leading into each curve like one thread of wire, so the heading carries the authority and the body carries the ease.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and open, its x-height soaring and every stroke cut to a ruler-straight width. And Noto Serif Malayalam adds a soft fat-and-slim modulation above it, so the sans body feels all the more constant by comparison.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-switzer: Switzer reads like tubular wire, with a tall waist line and tips that keep their distance from each other. Noto Serif Malayalam is best at moderate stem-to-hairline drama and dignified headings, while Switzer does its best work being smooth and free of any swell.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern and sturdy, its mean line set high and its joins as heavy as the stems around them. Over a longer stretch that plain sans settles into a steady, uniform texture, while Noto Serif Malayalam up top keeps a modest weight shift in each stroke.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-archivo: Archivo brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward rather than curling inward, a sans-serif with real editorial presence. But Noto Serif NP Hmong is what gives the pair its literary edge, with a faint thick-thin rhythm like crayon on rough paper.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-fs-asap: Asap reads openly, with arc-shaped c forms and a body height close to the capitals. Noto Serif NP Hmong earns its keep when set big and short, where its tall lowercase and quiet stroke contrast get room to show.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads curvy and unclamped, a wire-like monoline sans-serif with tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips. And Noto Serif NP Hmong sits above it with thin parts only slightly slimmer than its stems, so the two share a quiet, literary steadiness.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-fs-fira-sans: Tall, literary and wide-eyed, this pair starts with Noto Serif NP Hmong and its light touch of stroke modulation. Fira Sans then carries the text with zero thick-thin contrast and crossbars as fat as their stems, so a long passage feels uniform and unhurried.
gen-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong-fs-public-san: Trustworthy and editorial at once, Noto Serif NP Hmong has tall lowercase and thin parts that are clearly thinner yet never fragile. Public Sans backs it with a hefty, open-countered sans-serif body.
